Title: Felda settler dies in suspected axe attack
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: A Felda settler is believed to have been hacked to death with an axe by a man at Felda Lok Heng Selatan here after Maghrib prayers today.
A local source said the suspect was reportedly running amok by the roadside near his house while wielding a weapon believed to be an axe.
The source said nearby residents were afraid to intervene because the suspect was armed.
"Villagers did not dare to intervene because the suspect was holding an axe and running amok," the source said.
The suspect is believed to have fled on a motorcycle after the attack.
Kota Tinggi district police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman, when contacted, said a media statement on the incident would be issued tomorrow.
"The case is still under investigation," he said.
Earlier, a post about the incident went viral on social media, with some users claiming the attack occurred near their homes. Others alleged that the victim had been struck on the hand with an axe.

Title: UN probe accuses Israel of 'extermination' in West Bank
Article:
GENEVA: Israel has committed the crime against humanity of "extermination" in the West Bank, while continuing to commit "genocide" against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, United Nations-mandated investigators said Monday.
The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry said Israeli forces had also committed other crimes against humanity and war crimes in the West Bank, which Israel has occupied since 1967.
The commission, which does not speak for the UN itself, first determined in a September 2025 report that Israel had committed "genocide" in the war in Gaza following Hamas' deadly October 7, 2023 attack on Israel - a finding Israel flatly rejects.
In a new report – which comes the day before Israel's general election – the investigation found that in the West Bank, through military operations reinforced by sustained settler violence, Israel has waged a "widespread and systematic attack" against civilians.
"The Israeli authorities and forces have committed the crimes against humanity of extermination, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence in the West Bank, as well as persecution based on intersecting discriminatory grounds, with nationality, race and ethnicity at its core," it said.
Israel's mission in Geneva said the report was part of the inquiry's "misinformation campaign to demonise the State of Israel and portray its very existence as criminal."
"The international community must reject these distortions, repudiate the commission's findings and demand its immediate dissolution," it said in a statement.
The three-member investigative team was established by the UN Human Rights Council in 2021.
South African former High Court judge Navi Pillay, who chaired the investigation until November 2025, won the Nobel Peace Prize earlier this month.
The commission's new report focused on killings and bodily and mental harm caused by both Israeli and Palestinian security forces since October 2023.
It found that the situation in the West Bank has deteriorated gravely since the Palestinian Islamist group Hamas's attack from Gaza that month.
The commission found that the Israeli authorities "intended to collectively punish" West Bank civilians due to the Hamas attack.
"The targeting of Palestinian civilians across different locations in the West Bank indicates a high level of coordination and organised planning and is the product of state policy," the report said.
The conduct of Israeli authorities indicates that "they knew and intended settler violence" to be part of the widespread and systematic attack in the West Bank, it added.
"The intentional killing and injuring of Palestinian civilians and destruction of homes in the West Bank combined with Israel's persistent denial of responsibility form part of a broader strategy to exterminate and displace Palestinians and impose conditions of life that are unliveable," said commission chairman Srinivasan Muralidhar.
"Attempting to equate Palestinian statehood with a threat to the existence of Israel is blocking any viable attempts to realise Palestinians' right to self-determination," the Indian judge said in a statement.
The report cited cases where the commission concluded that Israeli forces intended to seriously harm and kill civilians, in acts which amount to war crimes including wilful killing.
The Hamas attack in October 2023 resulted in the deaths of 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.
Israel's military offensive, in response, has displaced nearly the entire population of Gaza and killed more than 74,200 people, according to Gaza's health ministry, which is under Hamas authority but whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
"The cases investigated for this report show that the Israeli authorities and forces continue to commit genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza," the report said.
The inquiry urged Israel to "end the commission of genocide in Gaza" and act immediately on "obligations to prevent and punish genocide and incitement to genocide."
Israel should "immediately end the unlawful occupation of Palestinian territory", and remove all settlers and settlements.
Turning to the Palestinian Authority, the report said that "Palestinian state violence has targeted and continues to target members of opposing Palestinian armed groups and repress Palestinian civil and political opposition."
The Palestinian Authority struggles with credibility and legitimacy, and "targets Palestinians who voice dissenting civil and political views... resulting in killings", it said.
"The Palestinian Authority has also failed to conduct prompt, effective and impartial investigations into incidents of killings."
There was no immediate reaction from the Palestinian Authority.
The commission is due to present its report to the UN General Assembly in New York on Monday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lufthansa returns to KL, plans daily Frankfurt flights in 2027
Article:
SEPANG: Lufthansa has returned to Kuala Lumpur after nearly a decade, restoring nonstop flights to Frankfurt with plans to increase the service to daily from the summer 2027 schedule.
The German carrier operates five flights a week using a 287-seat Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner equipped with its Allegris cabin, offering business, premium economy and economy classes.
Lufthansa Group senior vice president global sales Frank Naeve said the service reconnects two important cities and regions, creating opportunities for business and trade between Malaysia, Germany and Europe.
"With this new service, we are once again connecting two important cities and regions directly with each other."
"But a new route is much more than just connecting two points on a map. It very much follows the purpose of the Lufthansa Group, which is to connect people, cultures, and economies in a sustainable way," he said at Lufthansa's inaugural flight's arrival at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 today.
Naeve said Lufthansa will increase the frequency to daily flights starting next year's summer schedule.
"Initially, we have five services per week, but already today we have announced that we will operate daily services from the summer schedule 2027.
"So that very much reflects our commitment to this market and to connecting the two countries," he said.
He added that the route also strengthens Malaysia's air freight connectivity through Lufthansa Cargo, supporting trade flows between Europe, Malaysia and Southeast Asia.
"Let me also say one additional thing, the cargo contribution to these passenger services is extremely important in order to secure the economics.
"So that's why we're looking forward to a strong commitment also here in Kuala Lumpur for the cargo that we transport on these flights," he said.
Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) managing director Datuk Mohd Izani Ghani said Lufthansa's return follows sustained collaboration between the airport operator and the airline.
He said the direct connection carries economic significance for Malaysia.
"Germany is Malaysia's largest trading partner in the European Union, with extensive investments across various industries," he said.
Mohd Izani said the route also supports high-value exports by linking Malaysia's manufacturing hubs with Europe.
"This milestone represents close alignment across our government and industry," he said.
According to MAHB, Lufthansa's return brings KLIA's direct European network to five destinations served by five airlines.
KLIA handled 1.1 million passengers on European routes in the first nine months of 2026, up 29.7 per cent year-on-year.
German ambassador to Malaysia Silke Riecken-Daerr said the connection serves businesses seeking opportunities in both markets, as well as students, researchers, tourists and families travelling between the two countries.
She said Lufthansa's decision to return is a vote of confidence in Malaysia and gives fresh momentum to bilateral ties.
Deputy Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Chiew Choon Man said Malaysia recorded 1.18 million visitors from Europe between January and August 2026, an increase of 1.2 per cent from 1.16 million in the same period last year.
Germany accounted for 116,824 visitors during the eight-month period.
Chiew, who represented Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing at the event, said reliable air connectivity is central to Malaysia's efforts to attract international visitors.
"Strong and reliable air connectivity is fundamental to our efforts to attract more international visitors and ensure that Malaysia remains accessible and competitive in the global tourism market," he said.
He said Malaysia aims to strengthen its presence in the European market, encourage longer stays and create more opportunities for the tourism industry.

Title: M'sia committed to providing RM100mil in reconstruction aid to Gaza - Mohamad
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia remains committed to providing RM100 million in reconstruction aid to Gaza, as announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim last year, but its implementation has been hampered by the deteriorating security situation in the territory.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the aid would be implemented when conditions on the ground were more conducive, to ensure its effective delivery.
"To implement it, the situation on the ground is not permitting, because things there are not getting better. Instead, Israel is becoming more aggressive and is destroying Gaza," he said, when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 (Budget 2027) at the policy stage for his ministry, in the Dewan Rakyat, today.
Since 2023, a total of RM89 million has been channelled through the Humanitarian Trust Fund for the People of Palestine (AAKRP) to assist Palestinians in need, with more than RM12 million disbursed this year.
Meanwhile, Mohamad said that he would seek clarification from Myanmar over claims that about 300 of its citizens, who were repatriated from Malaysia, were still being detained by the military in Yangon.
He also said that he would instruct the chargé d'affaires in Myanmar to investigate the claim, and obtain information on the condition of those reportedly detained.
In another development, Mohamad said that the government would continue to use diplomatic channels to seek the Nepalese authorities' consideration of a request to declare the death of disabled climber Muhammad Hawari Hashim, who went missing while descending from the summit of Mount Everest three years ago.
He added that the effort also took into account a new ordinance, approved by Nepalese President Ramchandra Paudel on Oct 9, which allows victims of floods in Rasuwa district, including 54 Malaysians who remain unaccounted for, to be declared dead without having to wait for the 12-year period stipulated under the country's laws.
Mohamad said that the Foreign Ministry, through the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu, had raised the matter with Nepal's Ministry of Foreign Affairs via a diplomatic note on May 24, 2023, while a meeting with the Nepal Tourism Department was also held on July 7 this year, to seek consideration for the issuance of a death declaration for the climber.
He said that the ministry would continue discussions with the Nepalese authorities, and assist the family in obtaining legal services to apply for a court order on the matter.
On the West Asia crisis, he said that Malaysia continued to diversify its sources of supply, including crude oil and fertilisers, to reduce dependence on a single source, amid geopolitical tensions which had disrupted global supply chains.
Mohamad said the crisis had taught Malaysia the importance of having alternative sources to ensure that supplies of essential goods remained uninterrupted during conflicts.
Malaysia was also exploring opportunities to source phosphate from Algeria and Jordan, which could potentially work with local companies to produce the material for the fertiliser industry, he said.

Title: Longtime SJ Securities CEO Azman Manaf passes at 65
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Ahmad Azman Abdul Manaf, managing director and CEO of SJ Securities Sdn Bhd for 30 years, has passed away over the weekend. He was 65.
According to news reports, Azman was buried on Sunday at a cemetery in Shah Alam.
Azman joined SJ Securities as managing director in 1996. He also had a short stint in politics in the early 2000s where he served as deputy head of division for Umno Kuala Kedah.
He studied at the University of Reading, UK and obtained a degree in land management, valuation and estate management.
SJ Securities is a licensed broker regulated by the Securities Commission and Bursa Malaysia.
It was incorporated in 1985 and was formerly known as Subang Jaya Securities.

Title: Indonesian NGO alleges 21 Malaysian-linked firms involved in forest fires
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Indonesian environmental non-governmental organisation Wahana Lingkungan Hidup Indonesia (WALHI) has claimed that 21 companies linked to business groups with Malaysian ties were involved in forest and land fires in Indonesia between January and September 2026.
The findings are part of a mapping analysis report titled "Who Are Behind the Fires?" released by WALHI's National Executive.
According to the report, satellite data recorded at least 30,927 hotspots across Indonesia in the first nine months of this year, with nearly 50 per cent located within the operating concessions of oil palm plantation and forestry companies.
The regions with the highest concentrations of hotspots included West Kalimantan, with 9,529, and Central Kalimantan, with 7,141. The fires caused the Air Pollution Standard Index (ISPU) in affected areas to reach unhealthy to hazardous levels.
The analysis also found that at least 21 concession-holding companies in Indonesia with detected hotspots or fire incidents were subsidiaries of, or affiliated with, business groups originating from Malaysia.
Apart from Malaysian-linked companies, the WALHI report revealed that many other high-risk concessions were controlled by foreign capital and conglomerates with parent entities or registered shareholders in Singapore, Hong Kong and tax havens such as the British Virgin Islands and Samoa.
Meanwhile, on Oct 5, Greenpeace Indonesia and Pantau Gambut alleged that plantation companies from Malaysia and Singapore were among 20 entities linked to forest fires, based on a dataset of haze sources covering Aug 1 to Oct 1.
The report said some of the same Indonesian entities had also been identified in a 2019 report in connection with fires on land they owned.
WALHI said forest and land fires in Indonesia should not be viewed merely as technical errors or negligence by local companies holding permits.
Instead, it said the problem was structural, involving parent business groups that controlled operational policies and benefited economically from their control of the land.
The NGO called on the authorities and relevant ministries to take firm action, including reviewing permits, imposing administrative restrictions, suspending operations and revoking concession permits held by companies that repeatedly experienced fires in areas under their control.
It said the recurring pattern of hotspots across subsidiaries belonging to the same business groups showed that the fires were not isolated incidents caused by negligence among individuals on the ground.
Unity government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, on Oct 16, had said that
no Malaysian plantation companies
with oil palm concessions in Indonesia had been found to be involved in forest fires linked to the haze.
He said cross-checks with Malaysian companies showed that most of the fires observed had occurred outside concessions owned by Malaysian firms.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pahang Astro Awani journalist dies at 66
Article:
KUANTAN: Astro Awani senior journalist Mohd Zailani Md Atan, who was based in Pahang, died at his home here today.
Zailani, 66, died in his sleep about 5pm.
His wife, Suaibatul Aslmiah Abu Bakar, 52, said her husband had been unwell and had difficulty walking over the past few days.
"His condition improved slightly today, but he still appeared weak," she said.
She said her husband had high blood pressure and diabetes.
Zailani leaves behind a wife and four children.
He had been with the television news channel since 2007.
His remains were taken to the Saidina Ali bin Abi Talib Mosque in Bukit Sekilau for funeral prayers before he was laid to rest at the Setali Muslim Cemetery at 9pm.
Zailani's death came as a shock to many of his media colleagues, as he had appeared jovial and cheerful during a media dinner hosted by the Pahang Menteri Besar's Office on Oct 20.

Title: Two motorcyclists killed after car skids into opposite lane
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Two men were killed when the motorcycles they were riding were hit by a car that skidded into the opposite lane at Km 24.9 of Jalan Johor Baru-Gelang Patah-Pendas here.
Iskandar Puteri district police chief Assistant Commissioner Radin Ramlan Radin Taha said the accident occurred when the car driver lost control of the vehicle while negotiating a wet bend.
He said the car then veered into the opposite lane before crashing into the two motorcycles.
"Both motorcyclists, aged 34 and 50, were pronounced dead at the scene.
"They sustained severe head and leg injuries.
"Their bodies were sent to Sultanah Aminah Hospital for post-mortem examinations," he said.
Radin said the car driver and two passengers suffered minor injuries.
"The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for reckless driving causing death," he said.

Title: West River secures RM17.85m residential M&E subcontracts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: ACE Market-listed integrated mechanical and electrical (M&E) engineering services provider West River Bhd has secured two residential engineering subcontracts with a combined value of RM17.85 million.
The contracts comprise an RM11.0 million electrical works subcontract for a residential project in Puchong, Selangor, and an RM6.85 million air conditioning and mechanical ventilation (ACMV) nominated subcontract for Park Green at Pavilion Bukit Jalil, Kuala Lumpur.
Both contracts were secured via its wholly-owned subsidiary, West River Engineering Sdn Bhd (WRE).
The RM11.0 million fixed-price subcontract was awarded by China Construction Development (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd for a project along Persiaran Bandar Metro Puchong, Taman Mutiara Puchong.
Undertaken for Interpile (M) Sdn Bhd, the development features a 34-storey apartment block housing 526 units, along with a seven-storey podium containing parking facilities and a recreational floor.
WRE's scope encompasses electrical systems, associated infrastructure, testing and commissioning, technical coordination, quality assurance, and regulatory compliance. The works will follow the main contractor's construction schedule, with completion slated for Nov 17, 2028.
Separately, BUCG (M) Sdn Bhd issued WRE a letter of award for the RM6.85 million nominated subcontract at Park Green, Pavilion Bukit Jalil, undertaken for Regal Path Sdn Bhd.
The project comprises two serviced-apartment blocks totalling 453 units, basement levels, a 10-storey podium, and resident facilities.
WRE will oversee the supply, delivery, installation, testing, and commissioning of ACMV services and ancillary components under BUCG's master work programme.
West River managing director Lim Yong Lai said the two awards bolster the group's order book across two core disciplines.
"The Puchong project covers electrical works, while Park Green adds an ACMV package, demonstrating the breadth of our capabilities in supporting sizable residential developments," Lim said.
He added that the group remains focused on disciplined execution, quality, safety, and cost management, while continuing to pursue projects that align with its technical capabilities to drive sustainable long-term growth.
These latest wins follow West River's announcement on Oct 5, of a RM17.5 million subcontract for electrical, extra-low-voltage, security, and solar panel systems at E-Metro Logistic Park in Bandar Bukit Raja 2, Selangor.

Title: KKB's unit wins RM49.8mil arbitration against Shapadu Energy Services
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: OceanMight Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of KKB Engineering Bhd, has successfully secured a nearly RM49.8 million arbitration award against Shapadu Energy Services Sdn Bhd (SES), concluding a corporate dispute that first came to light in late 2023.
In a market filing today, OceanMight's parent KKB announced that its solicitors confirmed the receipt of the Final Arbitral Awards on Oct 21. The tribunal ruled in OceanMight's favor, ordering SES to pay a total combined sum of RM49.78 million.
The tribunal's decision, dated Oct 12, also carries a mandatory interest penalty. SES is required to pay a five per cent annual interest on the principal sum, calculated from the date of the award until the settlement is completed in full.
Following this decisive tribunal victory, OceanMight indicated it will now pursue necessary legal channels to ensure recovery of the funds, including seeking formal recognition and enforcement of the arbitral awards through the High Court.
OceanMight is a fabrication yard licensed by Petroliam Nasional Bhd for offshore facilities construction of lightweight fixed structures.

Title: Sarawak live pig imports to Selangor under strict controls since July 2025
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The import of live pigs from Sarawak to Selangor since July 2025 has been carried out with approved import licences and is subject to strict control procedures.
The measure aims to stabilise market supply and prices following disruptions to the pig farming industry caused by the spread of African Swine Fever (ASF).
Agriculture and Food Security Deputy Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin said the policy had been repeatedly communicated to the media and the Dewan Rakyat, and should therefore not be portrayed as a new measure introduced only this year.
"I deeply regret that allegations and accusations have been made without examining the facts, with some even attempting to link the issue to the Sultan of Selangor's royal decree and turn it into a controversy based on inaccurate information," he said in a statement today.
He said Sarawak Minister of Food Industry, Commodity and Regional Development Datuk Seri Dr Stephen Rundi Utom had announced the matter in July 2025 during an official loading ceremony at Pending Port, Sarawak.
Further clarification had also been provided by Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup, who was then Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister, and by Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu through oral question sessions and written replies in the Dewan Rakyat.
Chan said Selangor Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim had also explained that the state government allowed the issuance of import licences for live pigs from Sarawak, subject to strict conditions and control procedures. The animals are not permitted to stop at any other location and have to be transported directly to a slaughterhouse in Rawang.
"I was also informed that strict standard operating procedures (SOPs) have been established from the outset to ensure that the handling of livestock at Port Klang is conducted in a controlled and orderly manner.
"Among the measures imposed is the restriction of live animal unloading activities to between 8pm and 5am. The animals are unloaded using specialised cages before being transferred directly onto lorries for delivery to the slaughterhouse in Rawang," he said.
He said the procedures are to ensure smooth livestock transportation, minimise handling time at the port and reduce the risk of contamination and disruption to the surrounding environment.
Therefore, he said, claims that the operation had affected cleanliness and sanitation at the port should not be made without examining the SOPs and control measures in place, stressing that such allegations must be supported by facts and credible evidence.
Chan said he had conducted a working visit to a modern pig farm in Simunjan, Sarawak, in April to observe its operations and procedures for exporting live pigs to Singapore and Selangor.
"During the visit, I had the opportunity to observe the implementation of stringent biosecurity measures, including the use of livestock transport vessels that meet the stipulated specifications.
"These measures are important to ensure that livestock transportation is carried out in a controlled and orderly manner, taking into account animal health and risk management throughout the delivery chain," he said, adding that the issue should be discussed professionally and based on facts, rather than assumptions or inaccurate information.
He also hoped that all parties would refer to valid information and refrain from making statements that could cause confusion or unwarranted public concern.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia seeks Myanmar's explanation over 300 repatriated detainees
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will seek an explanation from Myanmar over reports that about 300 nationals repatriated from Malaysia remain detained at a military facility in Yangon.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia's chargé d'affaires in Myanmar would investigate the reports and provide an update.
"If there are reports that 300 people are still being detained, we will ask the Myanmar government to inform us.
"We will also ask our chargé d'affaires in Myanmar to investigate and tell us the situation.
"We will ask the Myanmar government to ensure the assurances it gave are honoured," he said in reply to Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman (PN-Sik) in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Tarmizi had asked whether the ministry was aware of media reports that about 300 Myanmar nationals, including Rohingya and ethnic Rakhine people, remained detained at the facility following the first phase of repatriation.
He also sought clarification on assurances given by Myanmar that the returnees would not face discrimination.
Mohamad said about 1,700 Myanmar nationals had returned voluntarily after signing documents confirming their intention to do so.
He said the Myanmar government had assured Malaysia of their safety, including during a recent visit by its representatives to Kuala Lumpur.
On Sept 29, Malaysia began the
first phase
of a repatriation programme involving 1,476 Myanmar detainees, who were sent home aboard three Myanmar naval vessels, including a hospital ship.
Home Ministry deputy secretary-general (Policy and Control) Datuk Makhzan Mahyuddin said the group comprised 1,370 men, 79 women, 20 boys and seven girls aged between 8 and 60.
The detainees were transferred from 14 immigration depots, with the largest groups coming from the Belantik depot in Kedah and the Tanah Merah depot in Kelantan.

Title: Ministry revokes 28,401 business licences over illegal activities by foreigners
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Housing and Local Government Ministry revoked 28,401 business licences nationwide over the past three years as part of efforts to curb illegal business activities by foreigners.
Its minister Nga Kor Ming said the ministry conducted 10,248 integrated enforcement operations nationwide to address the issue and protect the interests of local business owners.
"The operations resulted in 100,366 enforcement actions, comprising 65,023 compounds, 28,401 business licence revocations and 6,942 seizure and demolition actions involving business premises," he said in his winding-up speech on the 2027 Supply Bill in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Nga said the ministry took the matter seriously and had implemented strict enforcement measures to ensure compliance with business licensing requirements.
He also warned that local authorities would not hesitate to revoke the business licences of local licence holders who violated licensing conditions.
He said the Madani government remained committed to protecting local business owners and ensuring that business opportunities were accessible to Malaysians.
Meanwhile, Nga said 8,960 enforcement operations against littering were carried out in seven states from January to September under the Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Act 2007.
During the nine-month period, the ministry issued 17,145 notices for littering offences.
"Approval to prosecute was obtained for 2,883 cases, of which 820 had been concluded in court. A total of RM467,140 in fines was collected during the period," he said.
Nga added that community service orders totalling 3,638 hours were implemented during the period.

Title: Court of Appeal reduces Klang council's damages from RM117mil to RM3mil
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today reduced the damages payable by the Klang Municipal Council, now known as the Klang Royal City Council, to property developer NBC Land Sdn Bhd from RM117 million to RM3 million in a dispute over the rehabilitation of a former dumpsite.
A three-man bench comprising Datuk Ismail Brahim, K. Muniandy and Datuk Dean Wayne Daly also set aside nearly RM50 million in pre-judgment interest previously imposed by the Shah Alam High Court on the local authority.
Delivering the broad grounds of judgment, Justice Muniandy said the Shah Alam High Court was plainly wrong in principle and in law in the assessment of damages which warranted the intervention of the appellate court.
"The contractual damages flowing from the breach of the Dec 2, 2003 agreement must be assessed based on the works contemplated under the contract, namely the soil capping scheme estimated at RM6 million of which the appellant (Klang Municipal Council) was to bear 50 percent," he said.
Justice Muniandy said the agreement reached by parties was not an open warranty by the local authority to eradicate all waste or convert the dumpsite into virgin ground, rather the consensus was based on a specific proposal by the company's own consultant to execute an in-situ soil capping of approximately 1.5 meters of compacted soil over the waste, at an estimated cost of RM6 million.
"The parties agreed to share this estimated cost of RM6 million equally, 50 percent each (RM3 million each)," he said.
Justice Muniandy said that the High Court also erred in law in awarding the pre-judgment interest under Section 11 of the Civil Law Act 1956 as the award of pre-judgment interest cannot stand because the rehabilitation works were never executed and the landfill was also never excavated and third-party contractors were also not paid.
"To award nearly nine years of pre-judgment interest, amounting to approximately RM50 million, on an unspent, unliquidated estimate of works penalises the appellant (Klang Municipal Council) and produces an impermissible windfall," he said.
Therefore, he said the court substitute the High Court's award with RM3 million in damages, representing the council's agreed 50 per cent share of the RM6 million rehabilitation cost.
NBC Land acquired the land and obtained approval for residential development. It is not disputed that NBC Land knew at the time of acquisition that the land had been used as a dumpsite.
On Dec 2, 2003, following discussions between parties, an agreement was reached whereby the council agreed to carry out rehabilitation works in respect of the subject land and to bear 50 percent of the rehabilitation cost which was estimated at RM6 million. However, the council did not carry out the rehabilitation works.
In July 2020, the earlier panel of the Court of Appeal had held that the council was in breach of the agreement and remitted the matter back to the High Court for assessment of damages. The High Court proceeded to assess damages and in Feb this year entered judgment in favour of the company for RM117 million.
At the proceeding today, Tan Sri Tommy Thomas, Datuk Seri Nik Suhaimi Nik Sulaiman, Muhd Fadzli Amin Muhd Yusoff and Atiqah Azman represented the Klang Municipal Council while Harold Tan Kok Leng represented NBC Land. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RMAF gears up for first FA-50M fighters this Friday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) is prepared for the arrival of its FA-50M light combat aircraft, with the necessary infrastructure, personnel and maintenance support in place.
Its chief, General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris, said the designated squadron had been relocated, while its personnel had completed the necessary training to operate the air force's latest fighter aircraft.
"The No. 15 Squadron has been relocated to Kuantan Air Base, while pilots and technical personnel have undergone specialised training in South Korea.
"The first two aircraft are expected to arrive this week, while all 18 FA-50M aircraft are scheduled to be delivered by March 2028," he told the New Straits Times.
Earlier, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said Malaysia would receive its
first two FA-50M light combat aircraft on Friday
as part of efforts to strengthen its air combat capabilities.
Meanwhile, Norazlan added that the FA-50M, equipped with active electronically scanned array (AESA) radar, modern avionics, advanced targeting systems and precision-strike capabilities, will enhance the RMAF's air defence, combat training and strike capabilities.
"The aircraft would complement, rather than replace, the RMAF's existing Sukhoi Su-30MKM and F/A-18D Hornet fighter aircraft.
"The addition of the FA-50M would provide greater combat capacity and operational flexibility, allowing the RMAF to allocate its aircraft more effectively according to mission requirements," he said.
On the FA-50M's operational readiness, Norazlan said the timelines for achieving initial operational capability (IOC) and full operational capability (FOC) would depend on aircraft deliveries, personnel training, system integration and operational evaluation.
"We will ensure the aircraft meet the required operational standards before declaring the respective milestones.
"The acquisition of the 18 FA-50M aircraft is part of the RMAF's long-term modernisation efforts under the Capability Development Plan 2055 (CAP55)," he said.
In May 2023, the Defence Ministry and South Korean firm Korea Aerospace Industry signed a contract worth nearly RM4 billion for the procurement of 18 FA-50 Block 20 light combat aircraft, specifically designated as the FA-50M.
The variant was reported to be more advanced and capable than the FA-50s operated by the Republic of Korea Air Force and other nations including Thailand, the Philippines and Indonesia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UNHCR has failed to resettle refugees in third countries, says Mohamad
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) has failed to resettle refugees in third countries, says Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He said most Rohingya refugees in Malaysia held UNHCR cards, but the agency had resettled only about 5,000 refugees over the past two to three years.
"The majority of these Rohingya refugees are UNHCR cardholders.
"We asked UNHCR to send them to third countries, but UNHCR has failed to do so.
"That is why we are reviewing the presence of UNHCR in Malaysia," he said in reply to Datuk Muhammad Bakhtiar Wan Chik (PH–Balik Pulau) in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Mohamad said the agency should serve as a body that resettles refugees in third countries, as it did during the Vietnamese refugee crisis in the 1970s, but this was no longer happening.
He said many countries that usually accepted refugees, such as Australia, the United States and Germany, had closed their doors and adopted anti-immigrant policies.
Mohamad said repatriation was not an option as Rakhine State was no longer under the control of the Myanmar government.
He said it was now under the Arakan Army, whose violence against the Rohingya was even more brutal.
"Sending the Rohingya back means we are sending them back to be slaughtered.
"I will not agree. I state in this House that I will not agree to sending people to be slaughtered," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's invitation to Palestinian leader Abbas remains open
Article:
SLUG: OPENDOOR
Malaysia's invitation to Palestinian leader Abbas remains open
Amalia Azmi, Nor Ain Mohamed Radhi
news@nst.com.my
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's invitation to Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas to visit the country remains open, although a date has yet to be fixed.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said he had extended the invitation verbally on several occasions, and Abbas had expressed deep appreciation for Malaysia's support for the Palestinian struggle for a sovereign state.
However, he said Abbas had indicated that circumstances did not yet allow a visit to be scheduled.
"If I meet him again, I will invite him.
"If necessary, we will ask the prime minister to write a formal letter inviting him to Malaysia," he said in reply to Hassan Abdul Karim (PH-Pasir Gudang) in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Hassan had asked whether the government planned to invite Abbas, noting that Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and Jordan's King Abdullah II had visited Malaysia recently.
He also recalled that then prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad had invited Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) leader Yasser Arafat to Malaysia in 1984.
Mohamad said any invitation would be extended to the PLO, which he described as recognised by the international community, while Gaza is governed by Hamas.
"So, in answer to the question, if we are to invite anyone, we will invite the PLO, the government recognised by the world body," he said.

Title: Boy seriously injured after being hit at pedestrian crossing near school
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: An 11-year-old boy was seriously injured after being hit by a car while crossing the road outside Sekolah Kebangsaan Darau in Manggatal.
The boy sustained a head injury in the 6.10am incident and was rushed to Likas Hospital for treatment.
Kota Kinabalu district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrudin Mat Husain said preliminary investigations found that the accident involved a Proton Waja driven by a 69-year-old man travelling from Manggatal town.
He said the boy was crossing the road from right to left at the pedestrian crossing when the car approached.
"The driver was unable to avoid the boy due to the short distance and hit him in the right lane.
"The impact threw the boy forward before he was taken to hospital for further treatment," he said in a statement.
Shahrudin said the case was being investigated under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He urged those with information about the incident to contact investigating officer Sergeant Mazlan Mursalam at 012-3036605 or visit the nearest police station.
Closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage of the incident went viral on social media earlier, showing the boy being hit while crossing the road.
The footage showed the boy getting out of a Perodua Bezza on the opposite side of the road before crossing towards the school, where he was struck by a car and thrown forward.'

Title: Edelteq acquires 51pct stake in factory automation company Nixma
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Edelteq Holdings Bhd is acquiring a 51 per cent stake in factory automation solutions provider Nixma Technology (M) Sdn Bhd for RM15.3 million.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said it entered into agreements with Nixma's vendors on Oct 26 to acquire 15 per cent of the company's enlarged share capital for RM4.5 million and subscribe for new shares representing another 36 per cent for RM10.8 million.
The investment is expected to be completed by the fourth quarter of 2026.
Edelteq said the acquisition would strengthen its position in the semiconductor equipment and factory automation sectors by expanding its technical capabilities, product offerings, and access to an established multinational customer base.
Nixma designs and assembles factory automation products, including leak detection, assembly and testing, robotic, and high-precision automation solutions.
As part of the deal, Nixma's vendors have guaranteed a minimum audited profit after tax of RM6 million for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026. They must pay Nixma any shortfall if the guaranteed profit is not achieved.
Edelteq said the RM10.8 million proceeds from the share subscription would be used to build a new factory, purchase industrial land, or purchase suitable existing factory premises to support Nixma's expansion and production capacity.
Edelteq's shares closed 3.66 per cent or 1.5 sen higher today at 42 sen, valuing the company at RM248.96 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Britons top list of drug mule suspects arrested at KLIA, RM202.76mil in drugs seized
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 77 cases linked to drug mule syndicates at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) were recorded between January and Oct 15, resulting in the arrest of 93 people.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the cases involved the seizure of 2,526.28kg of drugs worth an estimated RM202.76 million.
He said the seized substances comprised 2,407.27kg of cannabis (64 cases), 77.837kg of methamphetamine (four cases), 22.11kg of ketamine (four cases), 15.585kg of cocaine (three cases), and 3.475kg of a ketamine and cannabis mixture (two cases).
"Of the 93 people arrested, Britons accounted for the highest number at 26, followed by Malaysians (23), Singaporeans (11), French (six) and Japanese (five)."
"Meanwhile, two people each were from Hong Kong, Indonesia, India, Ireland, Portugal and Germany, while one person each was from the Netherlands, Greece, Sweden, Slovakia, the United States, Brazil, Uganda, Zambia, Thailand and China," he said.
On the breakdown of the 77 cases, Hussein said 45 were recorded through cooperation with enforcement agencies, comprising 41 cases handled by the Aviation Security Auxiliary Police of Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd at KLIA and four by the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency.
"Another 25 cases involved action by the police and the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID), including the KLIA Narcotics Crime Investigation Division and the Selangor contingent police headquarters.
"Additionally, seven cases were recorded through follow-up operations, which led to the arrest of 12 people and the seizure of 571.59kg of cannabis flowers," he said.
Hussein said the results reflected the department's continued commitment, in collaboration with relevant enforcement agencies, to combating drug smuggling and curbing syndicates that exploit individuals as drug mules.
"The public is reminded not to be easily deceived by suspicious job offers or promises of lucrative rewards, especially those involving transporting luggage or items belonging to others to foreign countries.
"The public is also advised against carrying items belonging to others abroad without knowing their contents and to report any suspicious activities to the police," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: PH strategy pragmatic, but CM candidate needed
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan's focus on increasing its seats rather than reclaiming Melaka reflects a pragmatic electoral strategy, but its failure to name a chief ministerial candidate could weaken its appeal, analysts say.
Universiti Utara Malaysia political analyst Professor Dr Azizudin Md Sani said PH appeared to be prioritising winning as many constituencies as possible, with the question of who would lead the state government taking a back seat.
"It is a strategy, but one shaped by the reality that PH knows it faces challenges in securing a supermajority. Its target is therefore to win as many seats as possible in Melaka," he told the New Straits Times.
Azizudin said that while PH could delay naming its chief ministerial candidate, announcing one could strengthen its chances by giving voters a clearer leadership alternative.
In the 2021 state election, Barisan Nasional won 21 of Melaka's 28 seats, while PH secured five and Perikatan Nasional two, giving BN a commanding majority in the state assembly.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said yesterday that the coalition aimed to
increase
its representation rather than regain power, although he acknowledged the possibility of a hung assembly requiring a coalition government.
Adly, who served as Melaka chief minister from 2018 to 2020, said PH did not need a poster boy, urging candidates to focus on their respective constituencies.
Azizudin said PH's prospects would also depend on voter turnout and its ability to attract returning voters, urban professionals and the middle class, alongside the Malay support it was seeking.
"PH may be hoping to gain as much support as possible from outstation voters returning to vote, who look at national issues, as well as middle-class voters," he said.
Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said Adly's remarks reflected PH's recognition of BN's strong political position and the difficulty of overturning its dominance in the state.
"Therefore, PH is adopting a more cautious approach, focusing on defending its five existing seats and making limited gains rather than aggressively pursuing control of the state government," he said.
Tawfik said leadership was another factor, with PH yet to present a chief ministerial candidate with the same political visibility as Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
"Although Adly was a former chief minister, PH chose not to present him as its main leadership alternative, while BN also has prominent figures such as Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh and Mohd Noor Helmy Abd Halem," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thailand's Phuket hit by flash flooding and landslides [WATCH]
Article:
BANGKOK: Heavy rain has triggered flash floods and landslides on the Thai island of Phuket, with the weather authority forecasting more bad weather ahead of the end of the rainy season in the southeast Asian country, reported German Press Agency (dpa).
The town of Patong, a popular tourist destination, was among the worst hit. Floodwaters carried rocks, mud and debris into residential areas and shopping streets, damaging houses, shops and vehicles, the
Bangkok Post
reported on Monday, citing authorities.
After persistent rain, water and debris flowed down the hillsides into lower-lying areas overnight. The Kathu district, which includes Patong, was badly affected. Mud and boulders blocked sections of road, shop windows shattered and cars were flooded. In some areas, a driving ban was imposed.
Emergency crews moved in with bulldozers and other heavy equipment to clear debris and open drainage channels, while the city administration of Patong set up emergency shelters.
Disaster prevention authorities reported flooding in other southern provinces as well.
The weather service has warned that heavy rain is likely to persist until Wednesday at least, before the rainy season across much of Thailand draws to an end.
At the end of September, days of rain brought severe flooding to Thailand's capital Bangkok, prompting the city's administration to declare a disaster emergency in all 50 districts. Across the country, about 2.6 million people were affected, according to the authorities. – BERNAMA-dpa
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Asia Brands' non executive director Lim Weng Khuan passes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Asia Brands' Bhd announced the demise of Datuk Dr Lim Weng Khuan. He was 67.
Lim was appointed as an independent, non-executive director of Asia Brands on Aug 29, 2022.
He had over 34 years of experience in industrial relations and human resource management in Lion Group, F&N Group, HSBC Bank and Tan Chong Group.
Lim was a council member of the Malaysian Employers Federation and a member of the National Labour Advisory Council in 2018, 2020 and 2022 until September 2024.
He obtained a Bachelor of Laws from the University of London in 1988 and Certificate in Legal Practice in 1990.
Lim obtained his Master of Business Administration in General Management from the University of Hull in 1995, before obtaining a doctorate from the University of South Australia in 2005.

Title: Radzi hints at Umno return through Rumah Bangsa initiative
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: After nearly a decade away from Umno, Tan Sri Mohd Radzi Sheikh Ahmad has hinted at rejoining the party through its Rumah Bangsa initiative.
The development was shared by Radzi, a former Umno secretary-general, during a visit to the party's current secretary-general, Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, today.
"Not long from now!" he said, according to Asyraf Wajdi's Facebook post.
Radzi was active in politics during the administration of Malaysia's fourth prime minister, Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.
He also held several cabinet positions, including deputy minister in the Prime Minister's Department, deputy home minister and home minister.
The former Kangar member of Parliament later joined Bersatu and served as chairman of its Appeals Board in 2018.
Radzi, 82, the son of Perlis' first Menteri Besar, joined Umno in 1972 and won the Kangar parliamentary seat in 1982.
During the Umno crisis following the party election in 1987, Radzi was reported to have sided with Tan Sri Tengku Razaleigh Hamzah, who challenged Dr Mahathir for the party presidency.
The former Dewan Negara member later joined Tengku Razaleigh in establishing Semangat 46 before returning to Umno after the party was dissolved.
Tun Abdullah Ahmad Badawi, who succeeded Dr Mahathir as prime minister, appointed Mohd Radzi home minister in 2006.
In the same Facebook post, Asyraf Wajdi said the question about Radzi's possible return to Umno had been raised jokingly.
"Today, I was fortunate to receive a visit from a veteran Umno figure who has contributed greatly to the party. I gained a wealth of knowledge and experience from this meaningful meeting.
"His brief answer (about his intention to rejoin Umno) before leaving was enough to satisfy me in my efforts to bring back all former and new Umno fighters to strengthen Umno once again as a Rumah Bangsa," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia to push for Asean haze framework at Manila meeting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will table a non-paper on transboundary haze at the Asean Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Manila, the Philippines, on Nov 14.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the proposal seeks to establish a framework for Asean member states to support one another whenever forest fires or haze hit the region.
"I will bring a non-paper, not a formal agenda item as the Asean agenda has already been set, to the upcoming Asean ministerial meeting.
"I plan to propose discussions on establishing a proper framework to address transboundary haze, so that Asean member states can support one another whenever forest fires or haze affect the region," he said while winding up the debate on his ministry's 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Mohamad said he believed the matter could be resolved at ministerial level, provided there was mutual understanding and agreement.
He said the government was not sitting idle and had chosen to pursue soft diplomacy.
He said he had personally contacted his Indonesian counterpart then, Sugiono, as well as current Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir.
"Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had been in contact with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto to ask what assistance Malaysia could provide and how the situation was developing.
"Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi travelled to Jakarta to meet Prabowo and assured him that Malaysia was ready to help," he said.
Mohamad said the offer could not be put to use as visibility in the affected areas was less than 50 metres, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaching 1,000.
He said the fires were far from residential areas, making it difficult to put them out manually.
"Even so, the Indonesian government had deployed 17,000 armed forces personnel, alongside at least 60,000 volunteers, to fight the fires on the ground.
"Water-bombing was not possible as visibility was too poor, and international aviation regulations prohibit aircraft from flying when visibility falls below 300 metres," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Unitrade secures manufacturing rights for Finnish waste management tech in Johor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Building materials wholesaler Unitrade Industries Bhd is expanding its portfolio into the licensed manufacturing of semi-underground waste management containers following a new partnership with Finland's Molok Oy.
The group announced that its indirect 60-per cent-owned subsidiary, Winnson Ecotech Sdn Bhd, entered into a technology transfer and licensed manufacturing agreement with Molok on Oct 26.
Molok, headquartered in Ylöjärvi, Finland, is a waste collection solutions specialist and part of the European pre-collection waste management leader, SULO Group.
Under the agreement, Molok will transfer its manufacturing technology and know-how to Winnson Ecotech to locally produce the Molok Classic semi-underground waste collection container.
The licensed product is specified as a value-engineered 5m³ 2-hook hard container equipped with a lid. Molok will order and retain ownership of the rotomoulding tools and dies used for production.
As part of a 12-month transitional arrangement, Winnson Ecotech will initially purchase imported finished container units from Molok to meet supply commitments pending the commencement of local production.
To support the venture, Unitrade will provide a corporate guarantee to Molok to secure Winnson Ecotech's Euro-denominated licence fee and payment obligations.
Winnson Ecotech has been granted an exclusive, non-transferable, and non-sublicensable license initially for the state of Johor.
The agreement features a scalable expansion plan, automatically extending to cover all of Malaysia if Winnson Ecotech achieves its prescribed cumulative sales milestone in Johor during the first contract year.
Subsequently, the license will expand to Indonesia if the company meets its Malaysian sales milestone in the second contract year.
Simultaneously, Winnson Ecotech signed a distribution agreement with Blue Marble Sdn Bhd, as the exclusive distributor of the locally manufactured Molok Classic containers throughout Malaysia, which includes servicing the Johor State Smart Deep Collection System programme.
This strategic alliance is positioned to capture opportunities stemming from the Johor Smart Deep Collection System, an initiative being implemented by the Johor State government through Johor Corporation (JCorp) to replace conventional waste collection infrastructure with modern, semi-underground systems.
The license agreement carries an initial term of three years starting from the production commencement date, which is targeted for no later than March 31, 2027.
It includes an automatic renewal for two successive one-year periods, contingent upon Winnson Ecotech achieving cumulative minimum volume requirements.
The agreements are not expected to have a material effect on Unitrade's net assets, earnings per share, or gearing for the financial year ending March 31, 2027, but are projected to contribute positively to future earnings from the production commencement date.
Unitrade's managing director (MD) Nomis Sim Siang Leng stated the partnership is a vital step in developing new technical competencies within the group.
"Through this partnership with Molok, we are able to bring proven European waste collection technology to the Malaysian market while building local production capabilities that support more cost-efficient deployment, shorter lead times and stronger after-sales service," Sim said.
He added that the Johor initiative serves as an excellent starting point that could eventually scale across Malaysia and Indonesia as environmental awareness drives the adoption of sustainable waste systems.
"This partnership also aligns with our strategy to build earnings visibility in higher value-added businesses that are complementary to our existing verticals," he noted.
Molok's MD Teemu Kovero highlighted that Malaysia and Indonesia are key growth markets for modern waste management infrastructure.
"We are confident that Winnson Ecotech's local production capability, backed by the engineering expertise of Molok and SULO Group, will help set a new standard for semi-underground waste collection in the region," Kovero said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesian firefighters give thanks as rain arrives after four months [WATCH]
Article:
KALIMANTAN: After months of battling forest and land fires, fire-fighting volunteers in South Kalimantan, Indonesia, were moved to tears when rain finally fell, bringing relief to the fire-hit area.
A video circulating online shows the volunteers holding hands before prostrating themselves on the road in gratitude. They were still wearing their protective helmets, coats and trousers.
According to Tribunnews, the volunteers had spent about four months fighting fires near the border between Kaliukan and Sungai Alat villages in Astambul district, Banjar regency.
The rainfall came after more than 100 days without rain, during which dry conditions allowed fires to spread easily and made them difficult to contain.
Data for Oct 1 to 14 showed that forest and land fires had affected 1,754.30ha in South Kalimantan. Banjar recorded the largest affected area, at 530.61ha.
Heavy rain also drenched Banjarbaru on the afternoon of Oct 25, helping to extinguish fires and improve air quality.
Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency reported that air quality in Banjarbaru was classified as moderate on Oct 26, with PM2.5 the main pollutant at 28.8 micrograms per cubic metre.
