Title: Nepal turns to SMART’s drones, detection gear after declining two Malaysian rescue offers
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 26 — Malaysia’s third offer to assist Nepal in its search and rescue (SAR) operations for mud flood victims was accepted after two earlier offers were turned down, paving the way for the deployment of the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART), equipped with technical expertise and advanced detection equipment.
SMART commander Senior Fire Superintendent 1 Abdul Manaf Che Isa, who led the mission, said Malaysia initially offered to send 50 rescuers, followed by a second offer of 25 personnel with SAR equipment, but Nepal declined both offers because it already had sufficient rescue teams.
He said Nepal’s government eventually accepted Malaysia’s third offer, which involved deploying just 11 SMART personnel, nine high-capacity drones and specialised detection equipment, after several rounds of discussions.
“Our initial offer was to deploy 50 personnel for SAR operations, but Nepal had already deployed its own rescue teams and declined the offer. The Nepalese government needed specialised equipment and expertise that it lacked.
“At the same time, we did not want to travel there only to find that there was no work for us to do,” he said in a recent interview with Bernama on SMART’s humanitarian mission in Nepal.
According to Abdul Manaf, Nepal declined the first two offers not because it did not need Malaysia’s assistance, but because it had already mobilised enough rescuers, including members of the military, police and fire services, volunteers, and international SAR teams from countries including China and South Korea.
He said SMART’s strengths included high-capacity drones for aerial surveys, mapping disaster-hit areas and locating victims, as well as specialised equipment capable of detecting sounds and movement beneath mud deposits.
“Buildings may be buried beneath mud while their structures remain intact. The area may look clear from above, but this equipment enables us to detect sounds and movement. Such equipment was not available there, and the authorities saw the need for it,” he said.
Abdul Manaf said diplomatic engagement through the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu also played a key role in convincing the Nepalese military that SMART could provide the technical assistance needed, including SAR detection equipment, search cameras, satellite phones and specialised communication systems.
He said the Nepalese government prioritised self-sufficient international relief teams, a criterion that aligned with SMART’s capabilities recognised by the International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG), as disaster victims need local shelter, food supplies and logistical support.
Once Nepal’s government had approved the mission, the SMART team was deployed to the Nepalese military’s tactical base in Trishuli, from where it took a helicopter to reach search areas no longer accessible by road because of infrastructure damage.
Abdul Manaf said the mud floods had drastically altered the terrain, making existing maps unreliable and forcing SMART personnel to use drones, GPS, and physical observations to determine search routes.
“For ground operations, we could not rely fully on maps as the terrain had changed significantly from what they depicted. Roads and buildings had been destroyed, leaving only rocks, sand and mud,” he said, noting that mud deposits reached depths of three to five metres, and up to eight metres in some areas.
He said heavy rain and overcast conditions also hampered helicopter operations, forcing personnel to be dropped off on hillsides before walking for more than an hour to reach the operation site, while also facing the risk of further disasters.
He said SMART personnel spent three days conducting secondary searches with Nepalese military tactical teams in designated sectors between Timure and Syabrubesi, using their expertise and specialised equipment to search the last known location of the Malaysians reported missing, but found no survivors.
SMART also shared aerial images and drone footage with the families concerned and handed over equipment and supplies to the Nepalese military to support continued search operations.
Abdul Manaf stressed that the SMART team had searched as extensively as possible amid difficult geographical, weather and safety conditions, adding that SAR operations focused first on rescuing survivors, with recovery efforts undertaken if necessary.
He also appealed to the families to remain resilient and patient while awaiting further steps by the Malaysian and Nepalese governments through coordination by the Foreign Ministry. — Bernama

Title: Abang Johari confirms AI data centre plan in Sarawak under US$50b investment
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 26 — The US$50 billion investment announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim recently includes strategic plans by a major international company to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) data centre in Tanjung Embang.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said further details, including the name of the company involved, could not be disclosed at this stage to preserve the confidentiality of the corporate transaction.
“What the Prime Minister said is true, but it is still at the planning stage. There is indeed a proposal to invest in an artificial intelligence data centre.
“We cannot disclose the amount for now because it involves a top international company... We cannot reveal its name, but it is indeed there,” he told reporters after officiating at the Sarawak Urban Forum (SUF) 2.0 here today.
Earlier in his speech, Abang Johari revealed that the Prime Minister himself had contacted him to enquire about the entry of the world’s leading technology investor into Sarawak.
The Premier said the international technology giant had chosen Kuching as its investment destination because it viewed Sarawak as a forward-looking state that was aggressively transitioning towards a new economy.
“The topmost technology company in the world is coming to Kuching. Why? Because they see that we are forward-looking.
“Sarawak is transitioning to a new economy and we have prepared Sarawakians in terms of human capital. We provide free education, and that is why they like it because they know they will have good people to work with them,” he said.
On Saturday, the media reported that the Prime Minister had revealed that a global technology company had chosen Malaysia, including Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, for a US$50 billion investment in the AI sector. — Bernama

Title: Live pig imports from Sarawak to Selangor subject to strict controls since July 2025, says deputy minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The import of live pigs from Sarawak to Selangor since July 2025 has been carried out with import licence approval and is subject to compliance with strict control procedures to help stabilise market supply and prices following disruptions to the pig farming industry caused by the spread of African Swine Fever (ASF).
Agriculture and Food Security Deputy Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin said the policy had been repeatedly communicated to the media and the Dewan Rakyat, and should therefore not be portrayed as a new measure introduced only this year.
“I deeply regret that allegations and accusations have been made without examining the facts, with some even attempting to link the issue to the Sultan of Selangor’s royal decree and turn it into a controversy based on inaccurate information,” he said in a statement today.
He said Sarawak Minister of Food Industry, Commodity and Regional Development Datuk Seri Dr Stephen Rundi Utom had announced the matter in July 2025 during an official loading ceremony at Pending Port, Sarawak.
Further clarification had also been provided by Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup, who was then Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister, and by Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu through oral question sessions and written replies in the Dewan Rakyat.
Chan said Selangor Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim had also explained that the state government allowed the issuance of import licences for live pigs from Sarawak, subject to strict conditions and control procedures. The animals are not permitted to stop at any other location and have to be transported directly to a slaughterhouse in Rawang.
“I was also informed that strict standard operating procedures (SOPs) have been established from the outset to ensure that the handling of livestock at Port Klang is conducted in a controlled and orderly manner.
“Among the measures imposed is the restriction of live animal unloading activities to between 8 pm and 5 am. The animals are unloaded using specialised cages before being transferred directly onto lorries for delivery to the slaughterhouse in Rawang,” he said.
He said the procedures are to ensure smooth livestock transportation, minimise handling time at the port and reduce the risk of contamination and disruption to the surrounding environment.
Therefore, he said, claims that the operation had affected cleanliness and sanitation at the port should not be made without examining the SOPs and control measures in place, stressing that such allegations must be supported by facts and credible evidence.
Chan said he had conducted a working visit to a modern pig farm in Simunjan, Sarawak, in April to observe its operations and procedures for exporting live pigs to Singapore and Selangor.
“During the visit, I had the opportunity to observe the implementation of stringent biosecurity measures, including the use of livestock transport vessels that meet the stipulated specifications.
“These measures are important to ensure that livestock transportation is carried out in a controlled and orderly manner, taking into account animal health and risk management throughout the delivery chain,” he said, adding that the issue should be discussed professionally and based on facts, rather than assumptions or inaccurate information.
He also hoped that all parties would refer to valid information and refrain from making statements that could cause confusion or unwarranted public concern. — Bernama

Title: Court of Appeal slashes Klang council’s RM117m dumpsite damages bill to RM3m
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 26 — The Court of Appeal today reduced the damages payable by the Klang Municipal Council, now known as the Klang Royal City Council, to property developer NBC Land Sdn Bhd from RM117 million to RM3 million in a dispute over the rehabilitation of a former dumpsite.
A three-man bench comprising Datuk Ismail Brahim, K. Muniandy and Datuk Dean Wayne Daly also set aside nearly RM50 million in pre-judgment interest previously imposed by the Shah Alam High Court on the local authority.
Delivering the broad grounds of judgment, Justice Muniandy said the Shah Alam High Court was plainly wrong in principle and in law in the assessment of damages which warranted the intervention of the appellate court.
“The contractual damages flowing from the breach of the Dec 2, 2003 agreement must be assessed based on the works contemplated under the contract, namely the soil capping scheme estimated at RM6 million of which the appellant (Klang Municipal Council) was to bear 50 percent,” he said.
Justice Muniandy said the agreement reached by parties was not an open warranty by the local authority to eradicate all waste or convert the dumpsite into virgin ground, rather the consensus was based on a specific proposal by the company’s own consultant to execute an in-situ soil capping of approximately 1.5 meters of compacted soil over the waste, at an estimated cost of RM6 million.
“The parties agreed to share this estimated cost of RM6 million equally, 50 percent each (RM3 million each),” he said.
Justice Muniandy said that the High Court also erred in law in awarding the pre-judgment interest under Section 11 of the Civil Law Act 1956 as the award of pre-judgment interest cannot stand because the rehabilitation works were never executed and the landfill was also never excavated and third-party contractors were also not paid.
“To award nearly nine years of pre-judgment interest, amounting to approximately RM50 million, on an unspent, unliquidated estimate of works penalises the appellant (Klang Municipal Council) and produces an impermissible windfall,” he said.
Therefore, he said the court substitute the High Court’s award with RM3 million in damages, representing the council’s agreed 50 per cent share of the RM6 million rehabilitation cost.
NBC Land acquired the land and obtained approval for residential development. It is not disputed that NBC Land knew at the time of acquisition that the land had been used as a dumpsite.
On Dec 2, 2003, following discussions between parties, an agreement was reached whereby the council agreed to carry out rehabilitation works in respect of the subject land and to bear 50 percent of the rehabilitation cost which was estimated at RM6 million. However, the council did not carry out the rehabilitation works.
In July 2020, the earlier panel of the Court of Appeal had held that the council was in breach of the agreement and remitted the matter back to the High Court for assessment of damages. The High Court proceeded to assess damages and in Feb this year entered judgment in favour of the company for RM117 million.
At the proceeding today, Tan Sri Tommy Thomas, Datuk Seri Nik Suhaimi Nik Sulaiman, Muhd Fadzli Amin Muhd Yusoff and Atiqah Azman represented the Klang Municipal Council while Harold Tan Kok Leng represented NBC Land. — Bernama

Title: Zahid extends aid to two Bernama, NST journalists injured in Ipoh-Lumut road crash
Article:
IPOH, Oct 26 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has extended financial assistance and words of encouragement to two journalists from the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) and the New Straits Times (NST) who were injured in a road accident on the Ipoh-Lumut road yesterday.
The contributions were delivered today by his press secretary, Shuhaimi Mohamed, to Bernama journalist Nur Afiradina Arshad, 34, and NST journalist Zahratulhayat Mat Arif, 37, at their homes in Semenyih and Ipoh, respectively.
Speaking at Zahratulhayat’s residence in Klebang Harmoni, Shuhaimi said Ahmad Zahid had also pledged to monitor their recovery and provide further assistance where needed.
“We hope Dina and Zahra will recover quickly and be able to return to work. Their contributions extend beyond Bagan Datuk to the whole of Perak,” he said.
Several Perak-based media practitioners were also present.
Shuhaimi said Ahmad Zahid appreciated the solidarity and moral support shown by the Ipoh media fraternity towards the injured journalists.
He added that the deputy prime minister, who also chairs the Road Safety Committee, regularly reminded motorists to remain vigilant, particularly on poorly lit roads, and to prioritise their safety.
The two journalists were travelling from Ipoh to Bagan Datuk to cover an event scheduled to be attended by Ahmad Zahid when their Perodua Bezza was reportedly struck by a lorry in Menglembu.
Nur Afiradina was taken for treatment in the yellow zone of Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital as she sustained a neck injury, abrasions on her body, and a sprained ankle, while Zahratulhayat received outpatient treatment for minor injuries at the same hospital. — Bernama

Title: Dewan Rakyat Speaker asks Rayer to write formally over Takiyuddin’s ‘munafik’ remark
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Jelutong Member of Parliament RSN Rayer has been asked to write an official letter to Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul if he wants Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu) to be referred to the Parliament Rights and Privileges Committee.
Johari said that the committee will examine the matter regarding Takiyuddin’s use of the word “hypocrite” (munafik), which was linked to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the debate on the 2027 Budget last Monday, before making any decision.
“I will summon the committee to review it, and it will not be my decision afterwards. The decision will be made by the committee, which consists of members from both sides [of the house], and I will only announce it,” he said during the policy-level winding-up session of the Supply Bill 2027 (2027 Budget) debate in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Earlier, Rayer raised the issue under Standing Order 36(4), which prohibits members of the House from using unparliamentary language.
Johari explained that he had previously asked Takiyuddin to retract the word, but the PAS Secretary-General, via a letter dated October 22, suggested that a mediation process be held without retracting the word.
Johari also expressed disappointment when Takiyuddin subsequently made a statement to the media regarding the letter before he had the opportunity to respond.
Rayer stated that he complies with the rules of the House and believes Takiyuddin should do the same.
Last Wednesday, Johari said he had examined the Hansard before ruling that Takiyuddin must retract the word, either in the Dewan Rakyat or through a written explanation to the Speaker. — Bernama

Title: Melaka schools to remain open amid haze, outdoor activities suspended if API exceeds 100
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 26 — All educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Melaka will operate as usual tomorrow, said the Melaka State Education Department.
In a statement, the Melaka Education Department announced that outdoor classroom activities may proceed as usual in areas recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading below 100.
However, the department stated that all outdoor activities, including physical education, co-curricular and sports activities, camps, celebrations, assemblies, and activities in open halls, must be suspended if the API reading exceeds 100, in line with MOE Circular No. 1 of 2019.
“The End-of-Session Academic Assessment (UASA) will continue according to the schedule set by each school, including internal examinations.
“Schools are also urged to exercise due consideration for students unable to attend for health reasons, including permitting them to sit for the examinations at a later date,” the statement read.
The department also advised students to wear face masks, particularly those experiencing respiratory symptoms or belonging to high-risk groups.
“Parents and guardians concerned about the effects of the haze on their children’s health may choose not to send them to school, provided they inform the school.
“Parents, guardians, and all members of the education community are advised to refer to the Melaka Education Department’s official channels for the latest information on the operation of educational institutions,” the statement read.
Meanwhile, the Pahang Education Department announced in a statement that all schools in the state will operate as usual starting tomorrow, with any changes to be communicated from time to time through the respective District Education Offices. — Bernama

Title: Fuziah: PKR fields seven new faces among nine candidates for Melaka polls
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 26 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) is fielding seven new faces among its nine candidates in the upcoming Melaka state election, reflecting its push for leadership renewal.
Its secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the new faces make up 77.8 per cent of the party’s line-up, including four young candidates.
She said three women are also among the candidates, accounting for 33.3 per cent of the party’s total.
“Since the announcement of the candidates, I have visited eight state constituency election operations centres to assess preparations, meet campaign workers and help coordinate campaign machinery.
“These visits will continue until tomorrow to ensure preparations at the constituency level are progressing smoothly,” she said in a social media post today.
Fuziah said political renewal was not merely about introducing new faces but also about creating opportunities for the younger generation and women to take on greater leadership roles and represent the aspirations of the people.
On Saturday, Prime Minister and Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that the coalition would contest 21 seats in the Melaka state election next month.
Of the total, PKR will contest nine seats, while DAP will field candidates in seven and Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) in five.
The new faces fielded by PKR are Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri in Tanjung Bidara, Mohd Khuzairie Mohd Kamal Kannan (Rembia), Denesh Palasubraniam (Asahan), Datuk Azman Abidin (Paya Rumput), Muhammad Hakimin Mokhtar (Ayer Molek), Esma Eazreen Husin (Rim) and Muhammad Faiq Azman (Serkam).
The other two women candidates are former Machap Jaya assemblywoman Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin, who is contesting the same seat, and Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir (Kelebang). — Bernama

Title: British nationals top KLIA drug mule arrests, drugs worth RM202.76m seized
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — A total of 77 cases linked to drug mule syndicates at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) were recorded between January and Oct 15, with 93 individuals arrested.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said these cases involved the seizure of 2,526.28 kilogrammes (kg) of drugs, with an estimated value of RM202.76 million.
He said the seized substances comprised 2,407.27 kg of cannabis (64 cases), 77.837 kg of methamphetamine (four cases), 22.11 kg of ketamine (four cases), 15.585 kg of cocaine (three cases), and 3.475 kg of a mixture of ketamine and cannabis (two cases).
“Out of the total 93 arrests, nationals from the United Kingdom accounted for the highest number at 26, followed by Malaysia (23), Singapore (11), Japan (five), and France (six).
“Meanwhile, there were two individuals each from Hong Kong, Indonesia, India, Ireland, Portugal, and Germany and one individual each from the Netherlands, Greece, Sweden, Slovakia, the United States, Brazil, Uganda, Zambia, Thailand, and China,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
Regarding the breakdown of the 77 cases, he said 45 cases were recorded through the cooperation of enforcement agencies comprising 41 cases handled by Aviation Security (AVSEC) Auxiliary Police of Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) at KLIA, and four cases by the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS).
“Another 25 cases involved actions by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID), including the KLIA Narcotics Crime Investigation Division and the Selangor contingent police headquarters (IPK).
“Additionally, seven cases were recorded through follow-up operations, which led to the arrest of 12 individuals and the seizure of 571.59 kilogrammes of cannabis flowers,” he said.
Hussein noted that these successes reflect the ongoing commitment of the department, in collaboration with relevant enforcement agencies, to combat drug smuggling and curb syndicates that exploit individuals as drug mules.
“The public is also reminded not to be easily deceived by suspicious job offers or promises of lucrative rewards especially those involving the transport of luggage or items belonging to others to foreign countries.
“Furthermore, the public is urged to refrain from carrying items belonging to other people abroad without knowing their contents, and to report any suspicious activities to the police,” he said. — Bernama

Title: MACC seeks 24-year-old man to assist Sabah corruption probe, last traced to Semporna
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 26 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is seeking a local man to assist in an investigation in Sabah.
In a statement today, MACC identified the man as Jamaluddin Jamahali, 24, who is being investigated under Section 17(b) of the MACC Act 2009.
The commission said attempts to contact him and locate him at his last known address in Kampung Keramat, Semporna, Sabah, had been unsuccessful.
Anyone who knows his whereabouts or has relevant information is urged to contact investigating officer Abu Hudzaifah Abd Talib at 014-8573727 or via email at hudzaifah@sprm.gov.my. — Bernama

Title: Zahid rejects RM2.1b overspending claims, says ministry underspent revised allocation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today dismissed claims that his ministry overspent by RM2.1 billion, saying the figure reflected the difference between its original allocation and revised spending ceiling over three years.
Winding up the 2027 Budget debate in the Dewan Rakyat, Zahid said the ministry spent RM6.108 billion between 2023 and 2025, against a revised allocation of RM6.143 billion after additional funding was approved,
Free Malaysia Today
reported.
“When we compare the amended allocations, the ministry has in fact underspent,” he was quoted as saying.
The explanation follows calls by DAP Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng last month for the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission to investigate what he described as excess spending by the ministry.
The issue drew attention after Zahid voiced concern over delays in payments to contractors involved in ministry projects, saying some had been forced to cease operations because of cash flow problems despite completing their work.
Treasury secretary-general Johan Mahmood Merican later attributed the delays to the ministry's spending commitments, noting that most of this year's allocation for rural road projects had already been utilised.
According to Johan, spending on rural road projects reached RM1.8 billion in 2023 against an approved allocation of RM1.1 billion, RM2 billion in 2024 compared with RM1.3 billion allocated, and RM2.3 billion in 2025 against RM1.6 billion approved.

Title: Langkawi’s duty-free overhaul: RM300,000 vehicle price cap and RM10,000 spending limit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The duty-free status of Langkawi is not intended to allow wealthy individuals to keep luxury vehicles on the island for several years before bringing them into the Principal Customs Area to avoid paying higher taxes.
Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said changes to the duty and tax exemption policy for vehicles were introduced not only to address revenue leakage but also to discourage such business practices.
“At its core, this is a business model that we do not wish to promote, and we hope this policy will be accepted by all citizens,” he said in reply to a supplementary question from Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (PN-Langkawi) during the Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Mohd Suhaimi had sought clarification on the government’s review of the RM300,000 threshold for vehicle tax exemptions in Langkawi and called for stricter enforcement to prevent abuse of the facilities.
Liew acknowledged that some business operators would be affected by the policy but stressed that local residents would not be impacted.
Earlier, he said that, effective Jan 1, 2026, duty and tax exemptions for vehicles would be capped at a value of RM300,000 to prevent wealthy individuals from abusing the incentives to acquire luxury vehicles.
He said the threshold was reasonable and sufficient to meet the needs of local residents, car rental operators, taxi services and commercial vehicle users, while ensuring that the exemptions remained focused on vehicles used for daily activities and local business operations.
“Although there have been changes to the tax exemption policy for certain products on Langkawi Island, its status as a Duty-Free Island remains in effect,” he added.
Meanwhile, Liew said the government had announced in Budget 2027 an increase in the eligibility threshold for duty-free purchases by visitors and tourists from RM1,000 to RM10,000.
He said the revised threshold covered several additional categories of goods, including fashion accessories such as watches and handbags, electrical and electronic items, and textiles, while excluding tobacco products and motor vehicles.
“Raising the value limit allows both domestic and international tourists to spend more, which in turn generates a direct economic spillover for duty-free shop owners and local entrepreneurs in Langkawi.
“At the same time, the requirement for a minimum 48-hour stay will boost the hospitality sector, homestays, transport services, and the food and beverage industry, ensuring that economic benefits are widely enjoyed across the island’s entire tourism ecosystem,” he said.
Liew added that the government was also updating and expanding the list of Langkawi-made goods eligible for import duty exemptions when brought into the Principal Customs Area, increasing the number of items from 23 to 29.
He said the measure would particularly benefit micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Langkawi.
Both measures will take effect on Jan 1, 2027, he added. — Bernama

Title: Flight attendant charged over drunk driving crash that killed DBKL road crew on Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — A flight attendant pleaded not guilty at the Magistrate’s Court here today to two charges of driving under the influence of alcohol, causing the death of a supervisor and injuring a lorry driver in an accident on Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar here on Saturday (Oct 24).
Mohd Iman Nafiz Fong Mohd Sabirin, 26, is accused of driving with a blood alcohol concentration of 64 milligrams (mg) per 100 millilitres (ml) of blood, exceeding the legal limit of 50mg per 100ml, and causing the death of Faris Irfan Fazli, 29, on Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar heading towards Jalan Parlimen at 4.09 am on Oct 24.
The charge was framed under Section 44(1)(b) of the Road Transport Act 1987 (Amendment 2020), which provides for imprisonment of between 10 and 15 years and a fine of between RM50,000 and RM100,000, upon conviction.
If convicted, the accused may also be disqualified from holding or obtaining a driving licence for a period of at least 10 years from the date of conviction.
He also faces a charge of causing injuries to Ahmad Zakiyamani Zakaria @ Yusuff, 49, in the same incident.
The charge, under Section 44(1A)(b) of the same Act, carries a prison term of between seven and 10 years and a fine of between RM30,000 and RM50,000, as well as disqualification from holding or obtaining a driving licence for at least 10 years from the date of conviction, upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohamad Fadhly Mohd Zamry proposed bail of RM25,000 for each charge, with one surety, as well as the suspension of the accused’s driving licence and impounding of his passport, taking into account that he worked as a flight attendant and could pose a flight risk.
Defence counsel Mohd Anif Rafih applied for the bail to be reduced to RM15,000 for each charge. He did not object to the prosecution’s additional condition that the accused’s driving licence be suspended but opposed the requirement for his passport to be surrendered.
“My client needs his passport for work as a cabin crew member with a local airline. In addition, he is single and supports his family, including his father who requires regular hospital treatment for a heart condition.
“The defence proposes that the accused report to a police station once a month as an alternative to surrendering his passport,” he said.
Magistrate Atiqah Mohamed @ Mohamad Saim granted the accused bail of RM35,000 for both charges, with one surety, and ordered his driving licence to be suspended until the case is concluded. She also ordered him to report to the nearest police station once a month.
The court fixed Nov 30 for case mention. — Bernama

Title: Sepang eyes F1 return with Cabinet proposal due in November
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The Sepang International Circuit (SIC) is drafting a feasibility study on bringing back the Formula One (F1) Grand Prix (GP) to Malaysia, to be presented to the Cabinet in November.
SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif said it was currently holding engagement sessions with the government, relevant agencies and industry players to obtain accurate information and data for inclusion in the study.
He said the findings would serve as one of the factors for the government to consider before deciding whether Malaysia should return as host of the prestigious race.
“We are in the process of preparing a feasibility study of bringing F1 racing back to Malaysia. In November, we will present a proposal paper to the Cabinet for the government to decide whether to agree to the proposal.
“During this period, we expect to hold engagement sessions with the government, relevant agencies and industry players to ensure that the data presented is accurate,” he told Bernama recently.
Azhan Shafriman said the study would emphasise the economic impact of hosting F1, in addition to assessing the country’s level of preparedness, especially in terms of traffic congestion management and public transport facilities.
On the prospects of Malaysia returning as host of F1, he described the country’s chances as 50-50, as the final decision would depend on the government’s consideration of the study’s findings.
“For now, it is still 50-50. It’s difficult for me to say yes or no (whether it will happen or not). But, insya-Allah, we will provide verified data or information to help the government come to a decision,” he added.
Meanwhile, on the possibility of Sepang serving as an alternative venue for international races amid tensions in West Asia, Azhan Shafriman said the SIC had so far not received any approaches from countries affected by the conflict.
However, he said the SIC remains open to discussions should the need arise, taking into account the preparation time required to host a race.
Malaysia last hosted an F1 race in 2017.
After nine years, Sepang once again hosted an F1 race – the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 – from Oct 2-4 following the conflict in West Asia and an agreement involving Formula One, the International Automobile Federation (FIA), and the governments of Bahrain and Malaysia. — Bernama

Title: Pakatan ties, Perikatan disciplinary action on agenda at Bersatu meeting tonight
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 26 — Bersatu’s supreme leadership council is set to meet tonight to finalise, among other matters, the party’s political cooperation plans ahead of the 16th Melaka state election.
As reported by
Harian Metro
, the meeting, chaired by Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, is understood to begin at 8pm at the party’s headquarters in Petaling Jaya.
Sources said the meeting is also expected to discuss Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) decision last night to initiate disciplinary proceedings against Bersatu over allegations that it had acted contrary to the coalition’s interests.
Bersatu has recently been linked to a possible electoral cooperation pact with Pakatan Harapan (PH) for the Melaka polls. Both sides are understood to have held discussions, with PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari tasked with exploring the prospects of such an arrangement.
No official announcement has been made, however.

Title: Loke defends DAP’s seat reduction for Melaka poll as tactical shift for better odds
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 26 — DAP’s decision to contest only seven seats in the 16th Melaka state election, including its decision not to field a candidate in Bemban, was based on an assessment of its chances of winning, party secretary-general Anthony Loke said.
He said the decision took into account DAP’s performance in the 2021 state election, when the party finished second in several seats it failed to win, but came third in Bemban.
“We want to ensure that our strength, resources and focus are concentrated on seats we can win. That is why we are contesting only seven seats this time.
“It is a tactical and strategic decision by the party to ensure that our efforts and focus are directed towards the seats we can win, namely the seven we are contesting, including the four seats held by our incumbents,” he said.
Loke, who is Transport Minister, was speaking to reporters after officiating at a special financial assistance presentation ceremony for taxi, rental car and school bus drivers here today.
A total of 283 taxi and rental car drivers received RM1,000 assistance vouchers each at the ceremony.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, DAP’s Tey Kok Kiew, who contested Bemban under the Pakatan Harapan (PH) banner, lost to Perikatan Nasional (PN) candidate Dr Mohd Yadzil Yaakub by a majority of 328 votes in a five-cornered contest that also involved a Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate and two independents.
On PH’s strategy for the upcoming election, Loke said the coalition would focus on the 21 seats announced by Prime Minister and PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Saturday.
“We are working together under PH, comprising three parties – DAP, Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) and Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) – and we are focusing on the 21 seats we are contesting. We are not involved in the others,” he said.
PH is fielding 21 candidates from its three component parties in the state election, compared with 28 candidates in 2021.
The Election Commission (EC) has set Oct 31 for nomination, Nov 10 for early voting and Nov 14 for polling. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia targets bankruptcy discharges in under 36 days next year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The government aims to further shorten the processing time for bankruptcy discharges to less than 36 days next year to accelerate the financial recovery of individuals eligible for a second chance.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the initiative under the Fast Track Discharge Programme would be implemented through the Malaysian Insolvency Department (MdI).
She said the move was a continuation of the existing fast-track discharge programme, which enables eligible applications to be processed within 36 days, subject to conditions being met and no objections being raised.
Azalina said the government had also strengthened its recovery efforts through the Second Chance Policy, which recorded 253,457 bankruptcy discharges from 2023 to September 2026.
“These efforts will continue through the 2026 Fast Track Discharge Programme, which prioritises certain groups, including single mothers or fathers, micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) borrowers, fraud victims and purchasers of homes in abandoned housing projects.
“These measures will be supported by improvements to work processes, the expansion of digital services and stronger financial recovery mechanisms to help more eligible individuals obtain a second chance,” she said when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 (Budget 2027) at the policy stage for her ministry in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Azalina said the digitalisation of MdI services also enabled bankruptcy discharge applications to be submitted online through the e-Insolvensi portal.
Meanwhile, responding to a question from Datuk Mohd Isam Mohd Isa (BN-Tampin) on whether it was appropriate for a Member of Parliament to ask the Prime Minister to direct the Attorney-General to take action against certain individuals, Azalina said the proposed separation of the roles of Public Prosecutor and Attorney-General was among the measures to prevent perceptions of interference in prosecution proceedings.
She said the appointment mechanism for the Public Prosecutor, which had been debated in Parliament, would make the process more transparent while strengthening checks and balances on executive power.
“What we do not want is the perception that there is a ‘hidden hand’ behind any particular action,” she said. — Bernama

Title: High Court dismisses ex-student’s RM400,000 suit over phone seizure during SPM trial exam
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 26 — The Kuala Terengganu High Court has upheld the dismissal of a RM400,000 negligence and defamation suit filed by a former student against her teachers and the government over a body search and the seizure of her mobile phone during an SPM trial examination six years ago.
Judicial Commissioner Yusrin Faidz Yusoff dismissed Nur Nabilah Ahmad Zambala’s appeal and upheld a Sessions Court decision that threw out her suit against two teachers, a school principal and the government,
Berita Harian
(BH) reported.
The court ruled that while the school was entitled to confiscate Nabilah’s mobile phone, it had no authority under Education Ministry guidelines or school examination regulations to inspect its contents.
“Although the phone was indeed evidence, lawful possession of evidence does not automatically confer the authority to access its digital contents,” Yusrin was quoted as saying.
The case stemmed from an incident on October 25, 2020, when teachers conducted a spot check following complaints that Nabilah had cheated during a
Sains Rumah Tangga
SPM trial examination at SMK Sura in Dungun, Terengganu.
Checks on the phone uncovered notes, examination questions and answer schemes for several subjects.
However, Yusrin held that the procedural breaches did not amount to negligence, ruling that the teacher had acted reasonably in investigating allegations of cheating.
He also said identifying the source of the leaked examination questions and answer schemes was a more serious issue than the student’s possession of a mobile phone during the examination.

Title: Major legal win for Ampang Jaya residents as court allows challenge to council’s development plan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The High Court’s decision to grant leave to 12 Ampang Jaya residents to initiate judicial review proceedings challenging the Ampang Jaya Municipal Council Local Plan 2035 (RT MPAJ 2035) marked a significant step forward for local community rights.
In a statement, residents’ action group TOLAK RT2035 claimed that the local plan, gazetted on Feb 6, 2025, contained fundamental flaws and unpublicised land-use conversions.
They further claimed that the local plan did not incorporate the objections raised during the 2022 public objection hearing.
It said the court allowed the leave application, filed in May last year, after finding that the challenge raised arguable questions of law and fact warranting a full judicial hearing.
“We believe that the local plan currently permits high-intensity developments in environmentally sensitive areas on hilltops and hillslopes, and established disaster-risk zones.
“Unsustainable developments threaten terrain stability, escalate risks of severe landslides and flash flooding, and destroy the remaining natural environment,” the group said.
TOLAK RT2035 identified Bukit Antarabangsa, Taman Hillview, Ukay Perdana, Taman Melawati, Kemensah, and Taman Ukay Heights among high-risk zones facing pressure from proposed intensive and mega developments.
According to the statement, leaving the plan unchallenged would erode the public’s statutory right to object to future projects under the Town and Country Planning Act 1976.
The hearing for the substantive judicial review application has been set for Nov 25. — Bernama

Title: Pensioner charged in Kangar with sexual assault, using criminal force against two preteen girls
Article:
KANGAR, Oct 26 — A government retiree pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to three charges of committing physical sexual assault and criminal force against two girls about two months ago.
Annuar Abdullah, 72, entered the plea after the charges were read out to him before Judge Sharifah Norazlita Syed Salim Idid.
The first two charges alleged that Annuar committed physical sexual assault for sexual purposes against an 11-year-and-five-month-old girl at a house at No. 7, Lorong 4 Jalan Utama here, at 6.30 pm on Aug 11.
The third charge alleges that he used criminal force against a 10-year-and-11-month-old girl by pulling both her legs with the intention of outraging her modesty, at the same place, time and date.
The first two charges were brought under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
The third charge, under Section 354 of the Penal Code, carries a maximum prison sentence of 10 years, a fine, whipping, or any two of the punishments, upon conviction.
The court granted Annuar bail of RM10,000 with one surety and ordered him to report to a nearby police station on the first day of every month.
He was also prohibited from approaching or disturbing the victims and prosecution witnesses until the disposal of the case.
The court fixed Nov 24 for mention for submission of relevant documents.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohd Alif Farhan Hassan prosecuted, while Annuar was represented by lawyers Zuhair Ahmad Zakuan and Mohamad Alif Farhan Mohamad Supian. — Bernama

Title: Dr Mahathir absent from SG4 forum due to health issues, Mokhzani reads keynote
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad was unable to attend the SG4 Business and Economic Forum 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre today due to health reasons.
His son, Tan Sri Mokhzani Mahathir, said the 101-year-old statesman had prepared his keynote speech and intended to deliver it himself, but had been feeling unwell in recent weeks,
Berita Harian
(BH) reported.
“He worked hard on this speech and very much wanted to deliver it himself. Unfortunately, his health has not been at its best lately, and I am honoured that he asked me to present this keynote address on his behalf,” Mokhzani said when delivering the speech at the forum.
Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir was also present.
In the speech read by his son, Dr Mahathir apologised for his absence and said he had yet to make a full recovery, although he was grateful to still be able to share his views with participants through the prepared text.
No further details about his condition were disclosed.
Dr Mahathir, who serves as an adviser to SG4, had been scheduled to deliver a special address at the forum.

Title: AKPS rolls out hologram technology to help travellers navigate arrival procedures
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 26 — The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) has developed hologram technology to be deployed at the satellite building of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1, to assist travellers in obtaining information regarding arrival procedures in the country.
AKPS deputy director-general (management) Ismail Mokhtar said this initiative is part of the agency’s efforts to leverage technology to make it easier for travellers to access necessary information upon their arrival in Malaysia.
He noted that the development of this hologram was inspired by an initiative from the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN), which installed a hologram of the Minister of Home Affairs, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, in the lobby of the Setia Perkasa Complex.
“Just as the Ministry of Home Affairs placed a hologram of the Minister in the lobby of the Setia Perkasa Complex, AKPS shares the same vision and mission. We have created a hologram to be stationed at the KLIA satellite building, which will provide arriving travellers with information on the requirements they need to fulfil upon entry into the country,” he said.
He made these remarks while speaking at the AKPS 2nd Anniversary Celebration held here today, which was officiated by the Ministry of Home Affairs secretary-general, Datuk Dr. Awang Alik Jeman.
In a separate development, Ismail said AKPS aims to have 1,259 containers carrying electrical and electronic waste (e-waste) exported out of the country by the end of this year.
He explained that this target follows the government’s successful export of e-waste containers earlier this year, a feat achieved for the first time through a task force led by the agency.
“The issue of e-waste importation demonstrates that the threats at the nation’s entry points are becoming increasingly complex. Enforcement goes beyond merely detaining containers, it encompasses document verification, technical inspections, identifying the parties responsible, and monitoring follow-up actions,” he said.
During the event, AKPS also launched its 2026–2030 Strategic Plan, which serves not only as a reference document but also as an operational guide for its officers.
Additionally, AKPS unveiled a new logo featuring a red eagle symbolising the agency’s sharpness and state of readiness with a sundang (a traditional sword), representing courage and discipline.
Meanwhile, Awang Alik noted that the Minister of Home Affairs, who was initially scheduled to attend the celebration, could not be present due to an urgent, unavoidable assignment that arose at the last minute.
He mentioned that Saifuddin Nasution extended his apologies to all AKPS personnel for being unable to join in the celebration of the agency’s second anniversary.
“The Honourable Minister also expressed his apologies to everyone present today, as he was tasked at the last minute with an extremely important and unavoidable duty,” he said.
He added that the Minister of Home Affairs conveyed his regards, along with his congratulations and appreciation to all AKPS personnel, for their commitment and dedication in upholding the trust placed in them to safeguard the nation’s security and border sovereignty.
Earlier, the absence of both Saifuddin Nasution and AKPS director-general, Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, drew the attention of the press.
On October 21, Mohd Shuhaily was charged in the Magistrate’s Court with two counts of causing injury to two police officers.
He pleaded not guilty to the charges. The Sepang Magistrate’s Court has set November 25 as the date for the case mention and the submission of documents.
On October 24, Saifuddin Nasution reportedly said the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN) has entrusted matters concerning the position of the director-general of AKPS to the secretary-general of the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Chief Secretary to the Government, Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar. — Bernama

Title: Orang Asli in remote Kelantan and Terengganu areas urged to evacuate early as monsoon looms
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Oct 26 — Orang Asli living in remote areas have been urged to move to safe locations immediately if faced with the threat of floods, sudden torrents or landslides during the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), without waiting for conditions to become critical.
Kelantan and Terengganu Orang Asli Development Department (JAKOA) director Mohd Faedzyal Mohamed said all Tok Batin (Orang Asli village heads), penghulu (sub-district chiefs) and Orang Asli Village Development and Security Committees had been instructed to step up preparedness for the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon, which is expected to begin tomorrow and last until March next year.
He said the directive followed a statement issued by the Malaysian Meteorological Department on Oct 23, which forecast three to five episodes of continuous heavy rain between November 2026 and January 2027.
Mohd Faedzyal said village leaders needed to identify high-risk areas, monitor weather changes and river levels, and identify residents who might require immediate assistance during emergencies.
“These conditions could lead to flooding, particularly in areas near rivers and low-lying terrain. Residents must remain vigilant and prioritise the safety of themselves and their families,” he told Bernama today.
Mohd Faedzyal also advised residents to avoid using roads or bridges that were damaged, collapsed or eroded, and not to cross fast-flowing rivers or rivers where water levels were rising rapidly.
Sufficient supplies of food, clean drinking water, medicines and other essentials should be prepared, while important documents should be kept in a safe place in case evacuation became necessary, he advised.
Meanwhile, Galas assemblyman Datuk Mohd Syahbuddin Hashim said more than 1,000 Orang Asli heads of households in Pos Bihai, Pos Belatim, Pos Balar and Pos Hau were at risk of being cut off during the monsoon season because the dirt roads in the areas were vulnerable to heavy rain.
He said routes at Bukit Pasir, Bukit Kelabu, Bukit Sabun and Bukit Piyel needed regular maintenance to reduce risks to road users.
Mohd Syahbuddin also advised residents to avoid travelling during heavy rain and to contact JAKOA if they required emergency assistance. — Bernama

Title: Former Court of Appeal judge Mahadev Shankar dies at 94, leaves enduring legal legacy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Former Court of Appeal Judge Datuk Mahadev Shankar, renowned for his legal acumen, language mastery, and enduring contributions to Malaysian jurisprudence, died at Shah Alam Hospital at 2 am today. He was 94.
His close friend, Malaysia-India Heritage Society founder-president Prabhakaran Nair, said funeral arrangements would be announced later.
“Sadly, the Malaysia-India Heritage Society has lost a dear well-wisher whose friendship and goodwill we shall always cherish.
“His contributions to the Malaysian judiciary and involvement in the advancement of human rights, including his association with Suhakam (the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia), form an important part of his legacy,” he said.
Mahadev began his legal career in the 1950s and was appointed a High Court judge in August 1983 before being elevated to the Court of Appeal in 1994. He retired from the Bench in November 1997.
Born in Kuala Lumpur in 1932, Mahadev’s early exposure to the courts, coupled with a strong grounding in classical literature and languages, shaped a distinguished career spanning legal practice, judicial service and legal scholarship.
He began practising in Seremban before joining the law firm Shearn Delamore & Co, where he became a partner in 1961. He remained with the firm throughout his legal practice, handling a broad range of cases involving commercial and civil disputes, criminal law and medical negligence.
Mahadev was also recognised for his contributions to legal scholarship. An article he published in the Malayan Law Journal in 1984 on the distinction between putting a case to a witness and merely suggesting something to the witness continued to be cited by the Court of Appeal decades later.
His judgments covered issues ranging from employment disputes and damages in matrimonial cases to delays in the administration of justice.
In one ruling, he cautioned against delays that could leave litigants receiving their awards years later, when victory had become “academic or worse still pyrrhic”.
In a 2014 interview, he described judges as “tigers under the throne”, adapting a phrase traditionally associated with the judiciary’s role under the Crown to reflect the Malaysian context.
Some aspects of Mahadev’s legal career, scholarship and approach to the law were also highlighted by author and senior constitutional lawyer GK Ganesan in his article, ‘Is There Any Point in Learning Things by Heart’, in which he paid tribute to the late judge.
“He was one of the most learned men ever to sit on our Bench. Old English, Sanskrit, the Vedas, the whole of English literature: he knew them as other judges know their law reports. In that company, no judge in this country has equalled him,” Ganesan said. — Bernama

Title: Dr Akmal Saleh willing to sit out Melaka polls if court case hurts BN chances
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 26 — Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh says he is prepared to give up his bid to defend the Merlimau state seat in the Melaka election on November 14 if the court case he faces hurts Umno and Barisan Nasional’s chances at the polls.
According to
Berita Harian
, Dr Akmal said he had conveyed his position to Barisan Nasional chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, stressing that the party’s interests must come before his personal ambitions.
“If this case is seen as something that could tarnish the party’s image, I have told the Umno president that I am willing not to contest if I am considered a burden to the party’s chances of winning,” he was quoted as saying.
The 38-year-old said Umno had entrusted him with defending the Merlimau seat, although the final decision would only be known on nomination day. He added that he was also prepared to make way for another candidate if the party believed someone else stood a better chance of securing victory.
On August 22 last year, Dr Akmal pleaded not guilty to a charge under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code over a Facebook post allegedly causing public alarm. The offence carries a maximum penalty of two years’ imprisonment, a fine, or both upon conviction.

Title: Lynas waste disposal facility reaches 77pc completion as 2031 deadline looms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26  — The permanent disposal facility (PDF) for radioactive waste generated by Lynas Malaysia Sdn Bhd had achieved 77 per cent completion in construction and operations as of Aug 31, with 1.45 million metric tonnes of the 1.467 million metric tonnes of Water Leach Purification (WLP) waste generated having been transferred to the facility.
Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang said four disposal cells, designated A, B, C and D, had been completed, while the process of filling the facility with Auto Leach Residue (ALR) waste was ongoing.
“Based on monitoring by the Atomic Energy Department (JTA) up to Sept 10, radiation dose readings outside the PDF were also below 20 millisieverts per year, complying with the dose limit stipulated under Act 304 (Atomic Energy Licensing Act 1984) for radiation workers,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a question from Chow Yu Hui (PH-Raub) on the justification for renewing Lynas’ licence for 10 years, the status of the PDF, the amount of accumulated radioactive waste, and the mechanisms in place to ensure the company stops generating radioactive waste by 2031 and complies with all licence conditions.
Chang said Lynas was required to stop generating WLP radioactive waste before March 2031, while existing waste and waste generated during the period must be treated to reduce its activity concentration to below one becquerel (Bq) per gram using methods proven effective through research and development (R&D).
“This approach aims to reduce and eventually stop the generation of radioactive waste through recycling or reuse, while ensuring that mineral resources are managed sustainably and safely,” he said.
On who would be responsible in the event of a radioactive waste leak, Chang said Lynas was required to monitor the facility within the Lynas Advanced Materials Plant (LAMP) site during the first five years.
This was to ensure that the activity concentration of WLP waste could be reduced to below the control limit of one becquerel per gram stipulated under Act 304.
“Lynas must also continue its R&D on WLP waste, which will be monitored by the JTA. After the five years, if Lynas is still generating radioactive WLP waste, the JTA may suspend or revoke the licence.
“Therefore, the JTA will be responsible for ensuring that Lynas ceases generating radioactive waste by March 2031,” he said.
In March, the government decided to renew Lynas Rare Earths’ operating licence for another 10 years, allowing the Australian mining company to import raw materials containing naturally occurring radioactive materials and process rare earth elements (REE). — Bernama

Title: Loke says RM1,000 driver aid not a Melaka poll sweetener, rollout continues nationwide
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 26 — Transport Minister Loke Siew Fook has denied that the RM1,000 special financial assistance given to taxi, rental car and school bus drivers in Melaka today was intended to fish for votes ahead of the Melaka state election.
He said the incentive was being extended to all taxi, rental car and school bus drivers nationwide following its announcement by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the tabling of Budget 2027 in Parliament recently.
“I want to clarify some remarks made by people outside who have asked why the assistance is being given only in Melaka. The fact is that this special financial assistance is for all taxi drivers nationwide, not just those in Melaka.
“I am distributing the assistance in Melaka today. Last week, I was in Negeri Sembilan, and next week I will be going to Kedah. Taxi and rental car drivers in every state nationwide will receive this assistance,” he said.
He was speaking to reporters after officiating at the Special Financial Assistance presentation ceremony for taxis, rental cars and school bus drivers at the CMI Complex Auditorium in Ayer Keroh here today.
A total of 283 taxi and rental car drivers received contribution vouchers worth RM1,000 each at the event today.
Loke said about 12,000 taxi, rental car and school bus drivers were expected to receive the special financial assistance this week alone to help ease their financial burden.
“Those we were unable to invite to the ceremony will receive the assistance via electronic fund transfer (EFT) or direct bank transfers.
“The assistance is available nationwide. As long as they hold a valid driver’s card and its validity is verified by the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD), their names can be registered in the system and they will receive RM1,000.
“Starting today, we will also credit the assistance to the bank accounts of more than 12,000 recipients. We hope the funds can be disbursed as soon as possible to ease their financial burden,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Dr Akmal Saleh’s lawyers to file second representation after prosecutors reject bid to drop charge
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Oct 26 — Prosecutors have rejected a representation by Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh seeking to have a charge against him dropped, prompting his lawyers to submit a second appeal to the Attorney General.
His lead counsel, Aizat Azam, said the defence has applied to file a second representation to the Attorney General, setting out the facts and legal arguments relating to the case,
Sinar Harian
(
SH
) reported.
Speaking outside the Bukit Mertajam Court Complex today, Aizat said the first representation, filed in December 2025, was rejected and the decision conveyed during today’s case mention.
He said the case has been ongoing for more than a year, but no trial date has been fixed as the defence awaits a decision on whether the prosecution will proceed.
Dr Muhamad Akmal, 38, pleaded not guilty in August last year to a charge under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code over a statement allegedly posted on the Facebook page “Akmal Saleh” that was said to have caused public alarm and could incite offences against public order.
Aizat also told
SH
that the defence has filed a judicial review application against the Attorney General over his authority to prosecute the case. The matter remains at the case management stage, with a further online session scheduled at the Penang High Court tomorrow.
The Magistrates’ Court fixed January 4 next year for the outcome of the second representation.
The prosecution was led by state prosecution director Muna Mohamed Jaafar before Magistrate Roshayati Radellah.
Dr Muhamad Akmal was represented by a team of 10 lawyers.

Title: ‘No compromise’: Selangor exco backs police probe into drug stash at Klang temple
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 26 — The Selangor state government will not tolerate the use of any place of worship for criminal purposes, regardless of the religion, race or background of those involved.
Selangor Human Resources and Poverty Eradication Committee chairman V. Papparaidu said he took seriously media reports about drugs being found at an unregistered place of worship in Klang during an operation by the Selangor Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department from Oct 13 to 19.
“This case underscores the need for strict enforcement to combat drug distribution and the misuse of premises.
“Places of worship should be respected, kept sacred and provide peace to their respective congregations, not be used to store prohibited substances or facilitate criminal activities,” he said in a statement today.
Papparaidu, also co-chairman of the Special Committee on Buddhist, Christian, Hindu, Sikh and Taoist Affairs, stressed that there would be no compromise on using places of worship for criminal purposes.
“However, we must distinguish between the criminal actions of individuals and the religious institutions and communities they belong to. The actions of a few individuals should not be used as a reason to vilify or stigmatise an entire religious community,” he said.
He said the matter had nothing to do with religion or race, but concerned the rule of law, public safety and respect for the sanctity of places of worship.
“Criminal activities must be dealt with according to the evidence and the law, rather than sentiments or prejudices directed at any particular community,” he said, expressing support for the police in conducting a thorough investigation and taking appropriate action against those involved.
Selangor police busted a drug trafficking operation that allegedly used an unregistered place of worship in Klang as a storage facility, following raids across the state. — Bernama

Title: MoHE urges off-campus students to report residential addresses for monitoring
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The Higher Education Ministry (MoHE) has stressed that students living in rented accommodation off campus should inform their universities of their place of residence to facilitate monitoring.
Its minister, Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, said monitoring was difficult because some students arranged their own rental accommodation without going through their universities.
“So, that makes it rather difficult for us to monitor them. What we emphasise, however, is that they should always inform us of their whereabouts and where they are staying,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Dr Ahmad Fakhruddin Fakhrurazi (PN-Kuala Kedah) on the ministry’s proposal to work with state governments and property owners to provide student rental accommodation at controlled rates near public higher education institutions (IPTAs), pending the completion of new residential colleges.
Zambry said some public universities and polytechnics worked with their student affairs divisions to manage accommodation in designated areas, while some students opted to rent accommodation independently.
He said the proposal to provide student rental accommodation at controlled rates was also being considered to meet undergraduates’ housing needs, but its implementation would depend on the capacity of the universities concerned and their financial positions.
The proposal had also been raised by student representative councils, with several universities identified as requiring greater attention and priority in terms of student accommodation.
On targeted rental assistance for B40 students who failed to secure places in residential colleges, Zambry said priority was given to this group, along with students with disabilities, athletes and uniformed corps members, for hostel accommodation.
In reply to the original question from Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail (PH-Bandar Tun Razak) on efforts to address the shortage of accommodation at IPTAs, he said the government was working with government-linked investment companies (GLICs) to develop student accommodation facilities.
These included the Universiti Malaya Student Residence, which is expected to be completed in 2031 and benefit 10,000 students.
In addition, Budget 2027 announced a RM750 million allocation by the Retirement Fund (Incorporated) (KWAP) for the development of the Vista Kampus project at Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin (UniSZA) and Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), before it is expanded to six other universities.
Responding to a supplementary question from Dr Wan Azizah on incentives for the private sector to develop residential colleges, Zambry said MoHE, Finance Ministry, KWAP and the Public Private Partnership Unit (UKAS) were discussing ways to strengthen a hybrid public-private partnership (PPP) approach. — Bernama
